title: Naturality of the two jointly continuous coordinate formulas
statement:
Let $E$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a topology making addition, multiplication and inversion on $E\setminus\{0\}$ continuous. Let $J$ be a group with a topology making multiplication and inversion continuous. Let $V$ be an $E$-vector space with a topology making addition and scalar multiplication continuous, and with an $E$-linear $J$-action for which $J\times V\to V$ is continuous. For $n\geq0$ let $B_J^n(V)$ be the space of jointly continuous functions $F:J^{n+1}\to V$ with $F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_n)=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, and let $C_J^n(V)$ be the space of continuous functions $J^n\to V$, with $C_J^0(V)=V$. All finite powers have the product topology, and both spaces have pointwise operations. Write $P_n(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_n)$ and $r_n(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=(x_0^{-1}x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}^{-1}x_n)$. Put $\Phi_{J,n}F=F\circ P_n$ and $(\Psi_{J,n}f)(x)=x_0f(r_n(x))$, using empty tuples for $n=0$. Define
$$(\delta_J^nF)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^iF(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{n+1}),$$
$$(d_J^nf)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n),$$
with $(d_J^0v)(g)=gv-v$. Let $H$ be another topological group and $W$ another topological $E$-vector space with a jointly continuous $E$-linear $H$-action; define $B_H^n(W)$, $C_H^n(W)$, $\Phi_{H,n}$, $\Psi_{H,n}$, $\delta_H^n$ and $d_H^n$ by the same displayed formulas using $H,W$. Suppose $h:H\to J$ is a continuous group homomorphism and $u:V\to W$ is a continuous $E$-linear map such that $u(h(a)v)=a\,u(v)$ for all $a\in H,v\in V$. The formulas
$$b_n(F)(a_0,\ldots,a_n)=u(F(h(a_0),\ldots,h(a_n))),\qquad c_n(f)(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=u(f(h(a_1),\ldots,h(a_n)))$$
define $E$-linear maps $b_n:B_J^n(V)\to B_H^n(W)$ and $c_n:C_J^n(V)\to C_H^n(W)$ preserving the required continuity and equivariance, with $c_0=u$. They satisfy
$$b_{n+1}\delta_J^n=\delta_H^nb_n,\qquad c_{n+1}d_J^n=d_H^nc_n,$$
$$\Phi_{H,n}b_n=c_n\Phi_{J,n},\qquad \Psi_{H,n}c_n=b_n\Psi_{J,n}.$$
All four identities include degree zero. For $W=V$, $u=\operatorname{id}$ and the restricted action $a v=h(a)v$, that action is jointly continuous. No compactness, Hausdorffness or discreteness assumption is made.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-joint-continuous-coordinate-equivalence] to $(J,V)$ and $(H,W)$: their hypotheses are precisely the given topological field, topological group, topological vector space and jointly continuous linear action hypotheses. This supplies the pointwise vector spaces and the well-defined linear maps $\Phi,\Psi$. Apply [lem-sfb-joint-continuous-coordinate-differential] to the same two pairs to obtain well-defined linear maps $\delta,d$ with the displayed formulas. No comparison of iterated continuous-map spaces with product-map spaces is used.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, displayed differential including degree zero; agent-written naturality calculation for the explicit formulas of this item.

proof.text:
For each finite $k$, put $h^k(a_1,\ldots,a_k)=(h(a_1),\ldots,h(a_k))$. This is continuous: the inverse image of a basic open product $\prod_i U_i$ is $\prod_i h^{-1}(U_i)$; for $k=0$ both powers are points. Thus $u\circ F\circ h^{n+1}$ and $u\circ f\circ h^n$ are continuous, by composition. For $a\in H$ and $x=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$, the homomorphism law, equivariance of $F$, and the stated relation for $u$ give
$$b_n(F)(aa_0,\ldots,aa_n)=u(F(h(a)h(a_0),\ldots,h(a)h(a_n)))=u(h(a)F(h^{n+1}x))=a\,b_n(F)(x).$$
Hence $b_n(F)$ is in $B_H^n(W)$ and $c_n(f)$ is in $C_H^n(W)$. For either map $T=b_n$ or $c_n$, pointwise evaluation gives $T(\lambda q+\mu q')=\lambda T(q)+\mu T(q')$ from linearity of $u$. In degree zero $c_0(v)=u(v)$.

proof.text:
Deleting the $i$-th entry of a tuple commutes with applying $h$ entrywise. At $a=(a_0,\ldots,a_{n+1})$, linearity of $u$ therefore gives
$$(b_{n+1}\delta_J^nF)(a)=u\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i F(h(a_0),\ldots,\widehat{h(a_i)},\ldots,h(a_{n+1}))\right)=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i(b_nF)(a_0,\ldots,\widehat{a_i},\ldots,a_{n+1}).$$
This is $(\delta_H^nb_nF)(a)$, proving the homogeneous differential identity for every $n\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, displayed differential including degree zero; agent-written naturality calculation for the explicit formulas of this item.

proof.text:
For $n\geq1$, expand $u((d_J^nf)(h(a_1),\ldots,h(a_{n+1})))$. Pull $u$ through the finite signed sum by linearity, use $h(a_i)h(a_{i+1})=h(a_ia_{i+1})$ in each internal term, and use $u(h(a_1)v)=a_1u(v)$ in the leading term. The resulting expression is exactly
$$a_1(c_nf)(a_2,\ldots,a_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(-1)^i(c_nf)(a_1,\ldots,a_ia_{i+1},\ldots,a_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}(c_nf)(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
which is $(d_H^nc_nf)(a_1,\ldots,a_{n+1})$. For $n=0$, the same identity reads $u(h(a)v-v)=a\,u(v)-u(v)$, which follows directly from equivariance and additivity of $u$.

proof.text:
The identities $h(1)=1$ and $h(a_1\cdots a_i)=h(a_1)\cdots h(a_i)$ give $h^{n+1}(P_{H,n}(a))=P_{J,n}(h^n(a))$. Here the product identity follows by induction on $i$, starting with the empty product $1$ and applying $h(xy)=h(x)h(y)$ at the successor. Substituting into the two composites yields
$$(\Phi_{H,n}b_nF)(a)=u(F(h^{n+1}(P_{H,n}(a))))=u(F(P_{J,n}(h^n(a))))=(c_n\Phi_{J,n}F)(a).$$
For $n=0$ this is the equality $u(F(h(1)))=u(F(1))$.

proof.text:
Since $h(a^{-1}b)=h(a)^{-1}h(b)$, one has $r_{J,n}(h^{n+1}(x))=h^n(r_{H,n}(x))$. At $x=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$, use this tuple equality and the assumed intertwining equation for $u$ to compute
$$(b_n\Psi_{J,n}f)(x)=u\big(h(a_0)f(r_{J,n}(h^{n+1}(x)))\big)=a_0u\big(f(h^n(r_{H,n}(x)))\big)=(\Psi_{H,n}c_nf)(x).$$
The group identity used follows by applying $h$ to $aa^{-1}=1$ and then to $a^{-1}b$. In degree zero the ratios are empty, and the equality is $u(h(a_0)v)=a_0u(v)$.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, displayed differential including degree zero; agent-written naturality calculation for the explicit formulas of this item.

proof.text: For completeness, the degree-zero homogeneous differential identity of step 3 is $u(F(h(b))-F(h(a)))=u(F(h(b)))-u(F(h(a)))$, since $(\delta^0F)(x_0,x_1)=F(x_1)-F(x_0)$. Together with the explicit degree-zero equations in steps 4–6 and $c_0=u$ from step 2, this verifies all four identities in degree zero. Finally, when $W=V$ and $u=\mathrm{id}$, the restricted action map $H\times V\to V$ is the composite $(a,v)\mapsto(h(a),v)\mapsto h(a)v$. The first map is continuous in the product topology and the second is the given jointly continuous action. The action laws and linearity follow from the homomorphism law for $h$ and those of the $J$-action. None of these calculations invokes compactness, separation or discreteness.
